strengths.value: First PTQ method to reach near-lossless 3-4 bit compression with under 1% perplexity loss across LLaMA and Falcon scales.

ev.quote: SpQR is the first weight quantization method which is able to reach such compression ratios while inducing end-to-end accuracy error as measured in perplexity of less than 1%

strengths.value: Custom GPU sparse-dense kernel makes 3-4 bit SpQR 20-30% faster than FP16 inference on A100.

ev.quote: our specialized sparse matrix multiplication algorithm yields speedups of about 20-30%

strengths.value: Bilevel quantization of scales and zero-points enables very small group sizes (8-32) cheaply.

ev.quote: we quantize the groupwise statistics themselves using the same quantization algorithm as for weights

strengths.value: Provides hardware-targeted recipes mapping LLaMA size + bit-width to phones, laptops, RTX and server GPUs.

ev.quote: we provide a list of recommendations for the choice of the best LLaMA model and the corresponding compression level that fits into the device memory

weaknesses.value: Authors only measure perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, not actual generation quality.

ev.quote: we do not evaluate the generative quality of quantized LLMs, but only the predictive performance in terms of zero-shot accuracy and perplexity

weaknesses.value: Sparse and dense matmul are not fused, which leaves inference time on the table.

ev.quote: we do not fuse sparse matrix multiplication with regular quantized matrix multiplication. Such an approach would yield even better inference time performance

weaknesses.value: Outliers cost ~32 bits each (16-bit value + 16-bit column index), no compression of outlier indices.
